pull.title: KAFKA-21262: Wait for the share group and check the record count in share benchmarks
pull.body:
The first share group in a cluster has to wait for `__share_group_state`
to be created, which can take longer than the `--timeout` of the perf
tool. The benchmarks now read and release one record before the measured
run, and fail if the run reads fewer records than expected. Before this,
a run that read 0 records still passed.

`test_producer_and_share_consumer` writes one extra warm-up record, so
the consumer can read 1,000,001 records.

The tool side of the flakiness is fixed in #23781.

commit.message:
KAFKA-21262: Wait for the share group and check the record count in share benchmarks

The first share group in a cluster creates __share_group_state, which can take
longer than the perf tool timeout, so the tool read 0 records. Read and release
one record before the measured run, and fail if the run reads too few records.

+    def wait_for_share_group_ready(self, group, command_config, seed_record=False):
+        """
+        Wait until the share group can read one record from the topic.
+
+        The first share group in a cluster creates the __share_group_state topic. This can take
+        longer than the timeout of the perf tool, so it must be done before the measured run.
+        The record is released, so the measured run can still read it.
+        """
+        node = self.kafka.nodes[0]
+        common_args = "--bootstrap-server %s --topic %s --command-config %s" % \
+                      (self.kafka.bootstrap_servers(self.kafka.security_protocol), TOPIC_REP_THREE, command_config)
+
+        if seed_record:
+            node.account.ssh("echo warmup | %s %s" % (self.kafka.path.script("kafka-console-producer.sh", node), common_args),
+                             allow_fail=False)
+
+        cmd = "%s %s --group %s --max-messages 1 --release --timeout-ms 30000 2>&1" % \
+              (self.kafka.path.script("kafka-console-share-consumer.sh", node), common_args, group)
+        wait_until(lambda: "Processed a total of 1 messages" in self.kafka.run_cli_tool(node, cmd),
+                   timeout_sec=120, backoff_sec=1, retry_on_exc=True,
+                   err_msg="Share group %s could not read a record" % group)
+
+    def check_share_consumer_records(self, num_records):
+        records = sum(r['records'] for r in self.share_consumer.results)
+        assert records >= num_records, "Share consumers read %d records, expected at least %d" % (records, num_records)
+

issue.title: KAFKA-21262: Do not cap total run time in ShareConsumerPerformance

repository.name: kafka
repository.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

issue.body:
`--timeout` is documented as the maximum time between returned records,
but `ShareConsumerPerformance` also used it as a limit for the whole
run. A run longer than the timeout was interrupted and the tool printed
only the header line.

This is one of the two causes of the flaky share consumer benchmarks.
The other one is fixed in #23894, which should be merged first or
together: with only this change, a benchmark run that reads 0 records
still passes.
